Similarly, Ammonium chloride is linked to Kallikrein 14, which is a target of Taurocholic acid, and both of these pathways ultimately lead to the same target, Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, with varying degrees of support from different molecular pathways. The evidence suggests that Ammonium chloride may influence the activity of this transporter through different molecular intermediates, potentially affecting anion transport in cellular processes. The integration of these pathways highlights the complexity of the molecular interactions involved, emphasizing the need for further experimental validation to confirm the direct relationship between Ammonium chloride and the transporter.
